name: Trade job (branch root)
one_line: One piece of work for one client at one address, done by a tradesperson or a small firm: the enquiry, the quote, the diary slot, the before-and-after photographs taken on a phone, the materials bought on the way, the certificate issued at the end, and the invoice that closes it — usually inside a fortnight, often inside a day. Its defining property is SCALE, and scale changes the kind of object it is: there is no contract administration, no valuation cycle and no programme, the whole corpus of a job is a handful of files, and the anchor is the CLIENT AND ADDRESS rather than a contract. Its second defining property is that most of its files are machine-generated by a field-service app rather than authored. Absorbs the legacy row trade.job. Gist-level placeholder (J-IND): it recognises the situation and writes NO field rows, because the construction_property schema declares none.

deterministic: PRECONDITION: every entry below is a DETECTION signal and never an extraction licence. The construction_property schema declares no field rows (D1 as narrowed, _CONTRACT rules 10 and 15, CONNECTION PR-6), so nothing here writes a domain fact; detection exists so the material is recognised, kept where this row’s sensitivity says, and offered honestly. “Privacy policy must be enforced before content reaches any model or external connector.”

the field-service job document, which is this row's fingerprint: a machine-generated PDF carrying a job or reference number, a customer name and address block, a scheduled date, a technician or engineer name, a description of work carried out, parts used with quantities, labour time, a total, and a captured customer signature image at the foot. The customer-signature-on-a-work-record combination appears in no other row in this catalogue. “Tables matter because resumes, forms, applications, invoices, and administrative documents often place their most useful information in cells rather than body paragraphs.”

a small-job quote-to-invoice pair: a quotation and an invoice bearing the SAME reference number, the same address block and the same trading identity, differing only in tense and in whether a payment reference is present.

a phone-camera before-and-after pair: two or more images of the same fixture or room captured on one device within a short interval on one day, with camera EXIF present and frequently GPS. “Camera EXIF, GPS, and capture time can support deterministic photo-event proposals.”

a trading identity block repeated across every document: a sole trader or small limited company name, a mobile number, a tax registration number and a trade body membership logo, machine-stamped by the same software on quote, invoice and certificate alike.

a certificate issued at the end of a small job naming the same address as the invoice — the row's characteristic closing document, whose own detailed situation is construction_property.compliance-certificate's.
a card-payment or payment-link confirmation carrying the job reference — small trades are paid at the door, so the payment record is part of the job file rather than a separate accounting cycle.

an appointment record: a calendar entry whose labelled SUMMARY carries a customer name and an address and whose duration is a slot rather than a period. The CONTENT is what fires; source_type = calendar contributes only as a file-kind signal.
parent-folder context naming a customer, an address or a job number, treated as a clue once one of the structures above is present. Folder context never fires alone.
needs_llm: PRECONDITION: every file in this row names a private individual and the address they live at, usually together with a phone number and sometimes a photograph of the inside of their home. Any model step runs after P7 and under the user's policy. “Protected material should not be included in cloud-model prompts by default, should not display raw content in general group summaries, and should not be moved automatically without a user policy that explicitly permits it.”

the central determination for this row: separating a JOB from a PROJECT. The documents rhyme — both have quotes, photographs, certificates and invoices — and the discriminant is the machinery around them rather than the subject: no contract administration, no valuations, no programme, no packages, and a corpus of five files rather than five hundred.

separating the TRADE's copy from the CUSTOMER's copy of the same invoice and certificate. The documents are identical and the filing consequence is opposite: one is a business record about many customers, the other is a household record about one home.

an unlabelled job: a photograph of a handwritten quote on a duplicate pad, a text-message thread agreeing a price, and a bank notification — the commonest real job file in the trade world and the hardest in this row.
separating a job's before-and-after photographs from a household's ordinary phone photographs, which are the same device, the same day and often the same rooms.

a purpose-coherent job file whose members are individually unremarkable — a quote, two photographs, a materials receipt, a certificate and an invoice, sharing nothing but an address. “The documents are content-incoherent but purpose-coherent.”
in every case above, abstention is the required outcome where the evidence does not settle it. “A model that cannot cite sufficient evidence must return unknown.”
never_alone: a UK-style postcode or a street address alone. An address is the single most tempting token in this whole family and it appears in every role at once — the site, the client’s home, the contractor’s registered office, the architect’s letterhead, a supplier’s depot, and a comparable property cited in a report. 00 states the same ambiguity for a university name: “A university name alone should not create a group because Columbia can appear as an authoring school, course provider, target institution, employer, research venue, or merely a cited organization.” — the address case is worse, and this is recorded as inference because 00 writes that sentence about a university, not an address.

a person's name alone. In this row a customer name and a trading name look alike, especially where the trader is a sole trader trading under their own name — so the same token is the business and the client on two different documents.
an invoice structure alone. Invoices are the most format-standardised documents in the corpus and every schema in this roster has some.

camera EXIF alone on a phone photograph. A picture of a boiler is a job record, a household record, a warranty claim, an insurance photograph or an appliance the user was thinking of buying, and the image cannot say which. “conflicting signals should lead to abstention rather than an invented classification”
a job or reference number alone. Field-service software numbers everything sequentially, and the number is meaningful only inside the issuing firm's own system.
a trade word alone — boiler, rewire, leak, install, service. It appears in marketing material, in manufacturer manuals, in the user's own notes and in unrelated correspondence.

source_type or extension alone. “treat the file extension as a routing signal rather than an assumption about meaning”, and file_kind_plausible is constitutionally never-alone (CONNECTION section 5, invariant 2).
membership in a download session — a whole project folder or a document-portal export pulled down at once. “A session should never be treated as proof of topic”
a bare 4-digit number read as a year. It is at least as often a drawing number, a job number, a plot number, a house number, a cost code, or a British Standard reference.

a PDF author, producer, or company metadata string alone. “PDF metadata should be treated as supporting evidence, not as truth” — one contractor’s template stamps the same firm on every blank form it ever generated.

work_types: quotation or estimate for a small job
compliance or installation certificate issued at completion
grouping_reasons: one job for one client at one address — the definitional group in this row, and one that typically has five members rather than five hundred.

one client across several jobs over years — the boiler serviced annually, the landlord with four flats — a real reason to group, and the reason a customer name must never become an activation proof on its own.
one address across several trades' visits, which is how a homeowner's corpus is shaped even though the trade's corpus is shaped by client.
one job's photographs, joined by capture time and device rather than by any construction fact.
one quote across its revisions before acceptance, joined by the universal version_family fact.
no group at all is a valid outcome: a single materials receipt from a trade counter is an isolated transactional document.
and the stop rules apply as written — “when members carry irreconcilable course, institution, project, term, or purpose facts” — two customers' jobs in one folder do not merge.

template.why: Empty by binding contract: a dimension may only branch on a field the same entry’s schema declares, and construction_property declares none (D1 as narrowed, _CONTRACT rules 10 and 15, CONNECTION PR-6). That is a contract fact, not a claim that this situation has no shape — it plainly does, and it is recorded here as PROSE for whoever answers the schema row’s open_question. The recommendation, held as prose: the client or the property address first, then the job (its reference or its date and description), then the document function inside it — quote, work record, photographs, certificate, invoice — where a job has enough files to need one, which many do not. The client-or-address level is the row's real distinguishing recommendation: every larger construction row is organised by PROJECT and this one is organised by WHO and WHERE, because a trade's corpus is a list of customers rather than a list of contracts. A third function level should usually be FLATTENED rather than built, because a five-file job in a three-level tree is worse organised than a five-file job in one folder — 00's flattening allowance is doing real work here: “The system recommends an order based on the domain template, but the user can reverse, remove, add, or flatten dimensions.” 00’s own ordering reason applies: “a parent dimension should provide the context required to understand the child”. Not time-first — “For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders.” Time is a poor top level in particular, because a repeat customer's jobs scatter across years. And whatever eventually lands stays a recommendation: “The system recommends an order based on the domain template, but the user can reverse, remove, add, or flatten dimensions.”

collides_with.signal: The load-bearing collision on this row, and the one the row exists to draw. A job and a project share every document type — quote, photographs, certificate, invoice — and differ in machinery and scale. The discriminating evidence: an interim valuation, a certifying role, a programme, works packages or a retention regime supports the project row; a customer-and-address anchor, a single visit, a signature capture and a five-file corpus supports this row. Provenance: inference.

The quote is the sibling row's whole subject and this row's opening document, and in small trades a quote is often the ONLY document a job ever has. The discriminating evidence: a pre-acceptance document with a validity period, revised until accepted or forgotten, supports the quote row; a quote sitting in a completed job with a matching work record and invoice supports this row. Provenance: inference.

Materials receipts and paid invoices are simultaneously this row's job evidence and the trade's expense records. The discriminating evidence: a customer, an address and a job reference support this row; a merchant, a date and a total with no job anchor support the finance row. Because finance is a safety schema, where both fire the protective ordering runs first. Provenance: inference.

A trade's invoices ARE its sales ledger, and a field-service export is a bookkeeping export. The discriminating evidence: a per-job work record with a signature capture supports this row; a ledger, a period, a nominal code or a tax return supports the bookkeeping row. Provenance: inference.

Reciprocal with the landed household row. The customer's copy of a job's invoice and certificate is that row's home-maintenance record, and the trade's copy is this row's business record — the SAME PDF, filed by two people for two reasons. The discriminating evidence: many customers across many addresses supports this row; many trades across one address supports the household row. Stated reciprocally because neither can tell from the document alone. Provenance: inference.

A job's closing certificate is that row's whole subject, and it outlives the job by years. The discriminating evidence: a standard, a registration number and a next-due date on a document held for the PROPERTY supports the certificate row; the same certificate sitting in a completed job file with its quote and invoice supports this row. Provenance: inference.

Structurally the same object one schema over: one piece of paid work for one client, with a proposal, a delivery and an invoice. The discriminating evidence: a physical property address, materials and a site visit support this row; a scope of professional services, deliverables and no address support the career row. Provenance: inference.

A field-service visit report is byte-for-byte this row's job sheet in a different sector, produced by the same class of software. The discriminating evidence: an asset serial number, an equipment model and a service contract support the manufacturing row; a domestic or commercial property address and a trade support this row. Provenance: inference.

falls_through_to.why: Every job sheet names a private individual, the address they live at and often a photograph of inside their home, and a trade's corpus holds thousands of such customers who cannot consent. This is the row's default protective home. “Protected Records may represent sensitive isolated material such as passport scans, medical documents, account statements, visas, legal forms, or credentials; it should normally remain local-only and must not cause filenames or content to be exposed in model prompts.”

The row's most numerous member by far — materials receipts, card confirmations and isolated invoices with no job around them. “Receipts and Confirmations may hold isolated invoices, delivery confirmations, booking records, boarding passes, purchase receipts, event tickets, and similar transactional documents.”

The home for a standalone certificate or quote with a durable purpose and no job file around it. “Independent Records may live under Personal/Independent Records and hold standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group.”

The home for a single job photograph with no pair and no job around it — a very large population, because a trade's phone is mostly this. “One-Off Images may live under Photos/One-Off Images and hold images with no event, project, reference collection, or photo-family association.”

Screenshots of message threads agreeing prices and dates are how much of a small trade's contracting actually happens. “Temporary Screenshots may live under Photos/Temporary Screenshots and hold screenshots that appear time-sensitive or remind the user of something but have no accepted project, trip, application, or event relationship.”

The honest outcome for an appointment file or a customer export whose job and side are unresolved. “Review Later may hold files whose meaning is partly understood but whose final location requires a future decision.”

sensitivity_why: This is the construction row with the highest density of ordinary people's personal data per file. A single job sheet carries a named private individual, their home address, their phone number, their signature as a captured image, and a description of what is wrong inside their home; a trade's corpus contains thousands of them, and a set of before-and-after photographs is a picture of the inside of someone's house. 00's corpus sentence names the categories the moment they appear — the corpus “can include identity documents, account statements, tax records, medical information, legal records, credentials, private correspondence, GPS metadata, employment materials, and educational records”. As inference rather than a design claim, the exposed parties here are almost entirely NOT the user and cannot consent, which argues for the cautious setting even though each individual file looks mundane. This row assigns only the catalogue value potentially_sensitive; the handling class is P7's and is not set here.
open_question: Two. (1) The same-PDF-two-sides problem, stated reciprocally with the landed finance.household-property: an invoice and a certificate are the trade's business record and the customer's household record, identical bytes filed by two people for opposite reasons. Neither row can tell from the document alone; only the shape of the surrounding corpus can — many customers at many addresses versus many trades at one address — and corpus shape is not an activation input. This is recorded rather than resolved. (2) Whether this row should recommend a THREE-level tree at all. A five-file job in a three-level tree is worse organised than a five-file job in one folder, and 00 explicitly permits flattening. The honest recommendation is that the function level be offered and usually declined, which is a proposal about default behaviour rather than about evidence, and therefore Joseph's.
